headline: EQUINOX GOLD + ORLA MINING CLOSE: NORTH AMERICA'S NEW SENIOR GOLD PRODUCER — 1.1M oz/yr With Path to 1.9M oz; Jason Simpson Named Incoming CEO (TSX: EQX)
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) and Orla Mining completed their business combination on July 31, 2026 — formally creating North America's newest senior gold producer. Orla shareholders received 1.00 Equinox Gold share plus US$0.0001 cash per share. The combined entity is expected to produce approximately 1.1 million gold ounces annually, with a development pipeline providing a clear path to over 1.9 million ounces as high-quality North American growth projects are advanced; over 60% of initial production comes from three long-life Canadian mines. Leadership changes accompany the close: founder Ross Beaty moves to Chairman Emeritus and Special Advisor, Chuck Jeannes becomes Chairman, and CEO Darren Hall is retiring effective October 31, 2026 — with Orla's Jason Simpson stepping into the CEO role following a transition period. The deal creates material scale, operational diversification, and balance sheet strength at a gold price above $4,000/oz. For investors tracking the producer consolidation wave, this closure marks the largest gold M&A transaction on the TSX in 2026 and gives the combined company the institutional-quality size that typically precedes significant equity re-rating.

headline: NGEX LUNAHUASI: 20.50m AT 17.83% CuEq — 3.5m Of 20.25% Copper, 21.3 g/t Gold Cap Record Phase 4; Mars Zone Confirmed World-Class (TSX: NGEX)
snippet: NGEx Minerals (TSX: NGEX) released the final four drill holes from its Phase 4 program at the Lunahuasi high-grade copper-gold-silver project in San Juan, Argentina on July 30, 2026. The headline result: hole DPDH078 in the Mars Zone cut 20.50 metres grading 17.83% CuEq — including an extraordinary 3.5-metre internal interval of 20.25% copper, 21.3 g/t gold, and 172 g/t silver from 301 metres depth. Additional highlights include DPDH073 (34 metres at 3.03% copper, 1.89 g/t Au) and DPDH075 (13.50 metres at 5.74% CuEq). Lunahuasi is not a large-tonnage porphyry system — it is an extreme-grade underground target with Phase 4 confirming the Mars Zone as one of the highest-grade active copper-gold discoveries in the world. CEO Wojtek Wodzicki described the season as 'outstanding' and noted the results 'demonstrate continued upside.' The Lundin Group-backed company is expected to announce Phase 5 resource delineation drilling in Q3. For TSX investors tracking premium copper-gold discoveries, NGEX's Lunahuasi grade profile stands in a category almost entirely its own.

headline: RENFORTH PARBEC CHANNELS HIT 8.02 g/t Au OVER 2.55m — Open-Pit Assays Adjacent to Agnico Eagle's Canadian Malartic Confirm Unconstrained High-Grade (CSE: RFR)
snippet: Renforth Resources (CSE: RFR) announced surface channel assay results from the recently stripped Parbec Gold Deposit open pit on July 31, 2026 — the first channel sampling since the April 2025 Mineral Resource Estimate was completed. Eight channels were sampled across the stripped area; five returned gold above the 0.27 g/t Au cut-off used in the resource. Highlights: Channel 58 returned 8.02 g/t Au over 2.55m (including 28.77 g/t Au over 0.6m); Channel 51 returned 2.97 g/t Au over 10.2m — both ending in mineralization and unconstrained along strike and at depth. The Parbec deposit sits contiguous with Agnico Eagle's legendary Canadian Malartic Mine, and the results confirm the 2025 resource modelling — run at US$2,100/oz gold — was conservative at $4,000+ spot. Renforth is simultaneously advancing its 100%-owned Victoria Nickel-Copper-Cobalt-PGE polymetallic open pit deposit, adding critical minerals optionality to the same vehicle. For retail investors tracking near-surface, high-grade gold in established Canadian mining camps, Parbec is squarely in the conversation.

headline: WHITE GOLD CORP RUNS THREE DRILLS IN YUKON — Largest Diamond Drill Campaign In Company History Underway; Agnico Eagle Backing, PEA In Final Stages (TSXV: WGO)
snippet: White Gold Corp. (TSXV: WGO, OTCQX: WHGOF) released its mid-summer exploration update on July 29, 2026, reporting that 18 diamond drill holes totaling approximately 7,000 metres have been completed to date — with three rigs currently operating across the White Gold District in Yukon, Canada. The fully funded program is backed by strategic partner Agnico Eagle Mines and targets resource growth at the Golden Saddle, Arc, Ryan's Surprise, and VG deposits alongside new district-scale discovery. The 2026 campaign builds on exceptional 2025 intercepts: 56.10m at 3.23 g/t Au and 50.2m at 6.89 g/t Au at Golden Saddle. Critically, a Preliminary Economic Assessment is in its final stages — an updated economic document that WGO investors have long awaited. For investors following the Yukon gold exploration cycle, White Gold's 2026 campaign represents the highest-activity year in company history, with Agnico's strategic involvement adding an implicit acquisition premium that the current market cap has not fully priced in.

headline: BOLD VENTURES BURCHELL REE SYSTEM EXTENDS 3.2KM — New Outcrops Hit 3,060 PPM TREO; 29% Critical Magnet Rare Earths Confirmed Across Hermia Pluton (CSE: BOL)
snippet: Bold Ventures Inc. (CSE: BOL) announced on July 30, 2026 that fieldwork at the Burchell Project in northwestern Ontario has identified widespread Rare Earth Element anomalies in the Hermia pluton — a new discovery area located 2.2 to 3.2 kilometres east of the original discovery drillhole. Surface outcrops returned anomalies exceeding 500 ppm TREO, with a maximum of 3,060 ppm (0.31%) TREO across the new zone. The strategic context: earlier 2026 spring drilling at the main target returned 1,022 ppm TREO over 55.2 metres in a syenite-carbonatite host, with 29% of total REEs comprising magnet rare earths — specifically neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium, the precise elements targeted by US, EU, and Canadian critical minerals supply chain initiatives in response to China's dominance. The Hermia extension suggests the Burchell REE system may have a considerably larger footprint than initially outlined. A next-phase exploration program targeting the Hermia anomalies is planned. The project sits 100 km west of Thunder Bay — within trucking distance of established processing infrastructure.

headline: GLOBEX ROYALTY NETWORK PAYS OFF: ANTIMONY-GOLD IN NEW BRUNSWICK, HIGH-GRADE GOLD IN QUEBEC — Two Partner Drill Campaigns Deliver Simultaneous Results (TSX: GMX)
snippet: Globex Mining Enterprises Inc. (TSX: GMX) announced strong partner exploration results on July 31, 2026 from two properties under option and royalty agreements. Antimony Resources Corp. holds an option on Globex's Bald Mountain antimony-gold property in New Brunswick, reporting significant drill results from a Canadian project strategically important given China's October 2024 antimony export restrictions — which have sent global antimony prices sharply higher and made domestic North American deposits increasingly valuable. Emperor Metals Inc. holds an option on Globex's 50%-owned Duquesne West gold property in Quebec, reporting continued positive drilling results in the Abitibi gold belt. Globex's royalty-on-discovery model — the company holds royalty interests across 200+ properties in Quebec, Ontario, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia — means it collects exploration upside without carrying exploration capital risk. For investors seeking diversified exposure to multiple concurrent Canadian discovery campaigns through a single TSX-listed vehicle, Globex Mining is one of the most overlooked structures in the junior mining sector.

headline: COPPER CLOSES JULY UP 4% FOR THE MONTH, +14% YTD — Grasberg Restoration Slips to H1 2027; LME Inventory Falls, Structural Deficit Deepens For Junior Developers
snippet: Copper closed July 2026 approximately 4% higher for the month and 14% higher year-to-date, with LME three-month copper settling near US$5.99 per pound on July 31 after trading as high as $6.45/lb intra-week. LME exchange inventory has declined materially from April highs, and physical spot premiums continue to signal near-term delivery tightness. The lingering impact of the 2025 Grasberg flooding in Papua, Indonesia — which cut Freeport-McMoRan's 2026 production guidance by 35%, removing approximately 313,000 tonnes from this year's supply — is proving harder to remediate than initially projected, with restoration now estimated to extend into H1 2027. The IEA has separately warned that sulphuric acid shortages at global smelters put further copper supply at risk. Demand from AI data centres, EVs, and grid electrification continues to outpace 2024 consensus projections. For junior copper developer investors on the TSX-V and ASX, the sustained $5.50–$6.50/lb copper price environment significantly improves the project-level economics on development assets that were marginal at $3.50 copper in 2023.

headline: Q2 PRODUCER EARNINGS CLOSE WITH RECORD FREE CASH FLOWS — Historical Pattern Points to Junior Miner Re-Rating in H2 2026 as Capital Rotates Down the Risk Curve
snippet: With Q2 2026 producer earnings season effectively closed — DPM Metals (record $227M FCF), Agnico Eagle, Kinross, AngloGold, Endeavour, and now Equinox Gold all reporting strong beats or guidance upgrades — a historical capital rotation pattern is beginning to emerge. When senior gold producers report record cash flows at sustained high gold prices, institutional money tends to re-rate the sector in a predictable sequence: senior producer multiples expand first; mid-tiers get re-rated next; then junior developers and explorers receive fresh speculative capital as M&A competition drives perceived undervaluation at smaller market caps. In the current cycle, seniors are generating record FCF while still trading at discounts to NAV — suggesting the re-rating has not yet happened. When it does, the follow-on effect for TSX-V and ASX juniors could be material. Top analysts have noted that gold mining stocks as a class are currently pricing in long-term gold at $3,200–$3,800/oz — roughly 20% below current spot levels — creating what several major bank research desks are calling a historically compelling entry setup for investors willing to look past short-term equity market noise.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $84-87/LB AFTER $101 PEAK — Utility Contracting Accelerates; Wheeler River Under Construction, US Cost-Competitive Supply Years Away (NYSE: UUUU)
snippet: Uranium tracked between US$84 and US$87 per pound through Q2 2026 — approximately 15% below the January spot peak of US$101.41 — but the structural case for higher prices remains intact as utility contracting momentum picks up and new mine supply remains years from reaching market. Policy tailwinds are uniformly supportive: the US Section 232 framework classifies uranium as critical to energy security; the UK is building four new nuclear plants under the Hinkley framework; India and South Korea expanded nuclear capacity commitments in 2026. On Canadian supply, Denison Mines' Wheeler River Phoenix In-Situ Recovery project (final CNSC approval February 2026, construction commenced March 2026) targets 2028 first production — meaning utilities cannot rely on significant new Canadian supply for at least two years, and the July 2 resolution of the Peter Ballantyne Cree Nation's judicial review removes the last major social licence overhang for the project. Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU), the largest US uranium provider, reports Q2-2026 earnings on August 6, 2026, having already achieved its full-year uranium production guidance by mid-year at a mining cost of $23–$30/lb — a compelling cost structure at current spot levels.

headline: MACRO DATA DELUGE STARTS AUGUST 3 — PMI, JOLTS, Jobs, Jobless Claims Could Break Gold From $3,919–$4,237 Range; Junior Miner Catalyst Calendar Fills August
snippet: Gold enters August 2026 consolidating in a narrow $3,919–$4,237 per ounce range that has held since late June, with the first week of the month bringing a data-dense macro calendar that could force a decisive directional break. Scheduled releases include: July Manufacturing PMI (August 3), June JOLTS job openings (August 5), July Services PMI (August 6), initial jobless claims (August 7), and the July Unemployment Rate (August 8). Technical analysis shows gold in volatility compression — weekly momentum points slightly lower, but the absence of a decisive breakdown following the Fed's divided 9-3 hold in late July suggests the bull structure remains intact. July was a significant month for central bank gold demand, and any spot weakness is expected to be quickly absorbed by sovereign buyers. Beyond the macro data, the junior mining-specific catalyst calendar is also packed for August: Energy Fuels Q2 earnings call on August 6, and multiple TSX-V and ASX juniors are expected to release drilling results from summer programs in the Yukon, British Columbia's Golden Triangle, and Australia's Eastern Goldfields through mid-August.
